**T1 is going back to its builder**
- The builder says its 6 of 6 unit tests pass, but it made no commits and printed none as DESK lines either. So there is nothing on `change/add-greeting` to check against its report.

**Decision for you:** `pod.yaml` still lists two placeholder repos, `<repo-a>` and `<repo-b>`, with no real address or pin. ## Why

Users of `beta` want a greeting on start-up, and the text belongs in `alpha`,
the shared library, so that other tools can use it too.

## Scope

In: the greeting text in `alpha`; printing it in `beta`.

Out: translations; any change to `gamma`.

## Requirements

### R1 Greeting text
`alpha` SHALL provide the greeting `hello, demo` for a caller that asks for it.

#### R1.S1 Default greeting
- GIVEN `alpha` at the branch head
- WHEN a caller asks for the greeting with no name
- THEN it gets the exact text `hello, demo` (11 characters, no trailing
  newline)

#### R1.S2 Name too long
- GIVEN a name of 65 characters
- WHEN a caller asks for the greeting with that name
- THEN it gets an error naming the 64-character limit, and no greeting

### R2 beta prints the greeting
`beta` SHALL print the greeting from `alpha` as its first line of output.

#### R2.S1 Start-up line
- GIVEN `beta` built against `alpha` at the branch head
- WHEN `beta` starts with no arguments
- THEN its first line of standard output is `hello, demo`, within 1 s of
  start (wall time)

## Approaches

1. Greeting in `alpha`, printed by `beta` (picked: one source of the text).
2. Greeting in `beta` only (rejected: other tools would copy the text).

## Open calls

1. The name limit is 64 characters, counted as Unicode code points.

## 1 Goal and approach

Put the greeting text in `alpha` behind one function, and have `beta` print
it on start-up. Two build tasks, one per repo, with `beta`'s after `alpha`'s.

## 2 Interface contract

- `alpha`: `greeting(name: str | None = None) -> str`, in `alpha/greeting.py`.
  With no name it returns `hello, demo`. A name of more than 64 code points
  raises `ValueError`, whose message names the 64-character limit.
- `beta`: `python3 -m beta`, run in the `beta` checkout with the `alpha`
  checkout beside it, prints `greeting()` as its first line.

## 3 Global constraints

- "The name limit is 64 characters, counted as Unicode code points." (spec,
  Open calls 1)
- "its first line of standard output is `hello, demo`, within 1 s of start
  (wall time)" (spec, R2.S1)
- Every number carries its unit.

- alpha: `alpha/greeting.py` (the greeting and the name limit),

SKILL.md status-format.md # STATUS.md format `STATUS.md` sits at the root of a Project Space. The `swe-pod` skill builds it from the records, as read in `SKILL.md` section 1, and nobody edits it by hand (`PROCESS.md §15`). This file fixes its text, so two agents that build it from the same records write the same bytes. ## Layout The lines below are exact. Text in `` is filled in by the rules that follow; everything else is copied as written. ```text # Status: Generated from the records; never edited by hand. As of . - pins: , ... - open changes: (: , ...) ## state: owner: - gates: , ... - branches: change/: , ... - tasks: waiting , ready , dispatched , done , blocked | task | role | runs | state | latest | |---|---|---|---|---| | T | | | | | - latest evidence: , , : - open findings: Critical , Important , Minor - next: ``` One `## ` section follows the header for each open change, in byte order of the change ids, each with its bullets and task table in the order shown. For a sharded verify, the `latest evidence` bullet takes the sharded form given under "Per open change", with one indented line per shard. Blocks are separated by one empty line. No line has trailing spaces, and the file ends with one newline. ## Header - **Space id:** the `id:` value in `space.yaml`, such as `proj:demo`. - **As of:** the newest UTC, as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ`, among: - every ledger line under `changes/`, `changes/archive/` included; - the UTC that begins the name of each record under `changes/*/evidence/`, `handoffs/` and `decisions/`, written back with its dashes and colon (`20261102T1412Z` is `2026-11-02T14:12Z`); - the UTC on each `approved:`, `integrated:` or `abandoned:` line in a spec's header (`SKILL.md` section 1.2). With none of these yet, the line ends `As of no records yet.` - **pins:** each repo under `repos:` in `pod.yaml`, in the order written, as ` `: its name and the first 7 hex digits of its `pin`, joined by `, `. - **open changes:** `` is the number of changes in state proposed, approved, planned, building or verified. The parenthesis lists each of those states that has at least one change, in that order, as `: `, joined by `, `. With no open change the line is `- open changes: 0`. ## Per open change - **Heading:** the change id, its state (`SKILL.md` section 1.2) and the handle on the `owner:` line of the spec's header, separated as shown by three spaces. - **gates:** the gates passed, in this order: - `spec ` for each `approved:` line in the spec's header, in the order written; - `go ` for the ledger's go line (`go by ; ...`). A go line that names no handle gives `go `. With none passed, the bullet is `- gates: none`. - **branches:** before the go line, `- branches: none yet`. After it, each repo in the spec's `repos:` list, in that order, as ` `, the head of `change/` by the Branch head rule (`SKILL.md` section 1.1): read from the remote when the remote can be read, and from the records when it cannot. A repo with no head by that rule is ` missing`. - **tasks:** the number of tasks in each task state, in the order shown, zeros included. / pass`, where `` counts the test files in `changes//tests/` that map to that key (`SKILL.md` section 5, step 4), each only when `` is not 0. For a sharded verify (`SKILL.md` section 1.7), the bullet shows each shard's latest record, one indented line per shard, in task order: ```text - latest evidence: sharded, : - : , , [, stale]: - : none ``` - The first line is `green` when the shards' latest records are green together (`SKILL.md` section 1.7). Its results are those above, over the latest records taken together: a result is a pass when one of them passes it and none gives it `fail` or `not-run`. A repo's `unit` is `fail` when one of them gives `fail`, else the first of `pass` and `none-present` that one of them gives, else `missing`. - A shard's line is `: none` until the shard has a record. Its results are those above, but each `` counts only the results of that kind the record gives, and a kind it gives none of is left out: `unit` for each repo the record lists, in the spec's `repos:` order, and `quality none-declared` when the record says so. - **open findings:** the totals of section "Open findings", below. - **next:** one of these, by the change's state: | State | `next:` | |---|---| | proposed | `next: approval of changes//spec.md, by the human` | | approved | `next: the plan, by the plan role` | | planned | `next: the go, by the human` | | building, verified | the first ready task, as `next: T -> (, )`, with `runs:` and `needs:` from the plan | When a building or verified change has no ready task, the first of these that holds gives the bullet: - a verify shard is done and its latest record is out of date (`SKILL.md` section 1.7): `next: re-run T[, T] at the current commit set`, naming each such shard in task order; - every task is done: `next: none; every task is done`; - otherwise: `next: none ready; dispatched: T, T`, adding `; blocked: T` when any task is blocked and leaving out a list that would be empty. ## The task table One row per plan task (`SKILL.md` section 1.3), in task order: by number, with a letter suffix after the bare number (`T19`, `T19a`, `T19b`, `T20`). - **task:** the id, `T`. - **role:** the first word of the task's `role:` field. - **runs:** `local` or `mesh`, from its `runs:` field. - **state:** one of the five task states, below. - **latest:** the task's newest event, as below, or `-` when it has none. ### Task states Decide each task's state by the first of these that holds. The ledger terms (reported, review closed, held) are defined in `SKILL.md` section 1.4. 1. **done.** - A build task: it has reported, and its review is closed. - A review task: the review of the task it reviews (`SKILL.md` section 1.3) is closed. A review task too is dispatched only by its own dispatch line. 4. **ready.** It is not held, and every task in its `after` list is done. A review task that reviews one task is ready instead once that task has reported and every other task in its `after` list is done, since the review is part of that task's done-when. 5. **waiting.** Anything else, held tasks included. ### Latest A task's events are the dispatch, status, fix-round, at-base and returned-to-test lines that name it. A review task's events are its own dispatch lines and the review lines of the task it reviews (its own review lines, when it reviews no single task). The newest is the one with the latest UTC, and of those the one written last. The cell is its UTC, a space, and the event in this form: | Event | Cell text after the UTC | |---|---| | dispatch | `dispatch -> (, )` | | status | the status word, then `, ..` and `, unit

/ pass` when the line has them in that form; nothing else | | in words, that the task is finished, done or complete (`SKILL.md` section 1.4) | `DONE` | | review | `review: ` or `review r: `, then `spec ok` or `spec issues`, then `; ` and its counts as ` ` in the order Critical, Important, Minor, joined by `, `, without file and line. Leave out each count of 0. When no count is left, or the line gives none, write `none`: `spec ok; 0 Important` gives `review: spec ok; none` | | fix round | `fix round /5: addressed, open` | | at base | `at base: fail,

pass`, counting the tests the line names | | returned to test | `returned to test: ` | A `|` inside a cell is written `\|`. ## Open findings The ledger's review and fix-round lines give the counts. - **Critical and Important.** For each task that has a review line, take its newest review or fix-round line. A review line gives its Critical and Important counts. A fix-round line gives its ` open` findings, counted as Critical up to the number of Critical findings in the review before it, and the rest as Important. A ruling closes them at any round: when a `Ruling:` line newer than that line begins `Ruling: T open findings`, as in `Ruling: T open findings parked: ; ; `, the task counts 0.
